move: huge halftone-screened number wipes in top-down and counts up on cream poster
how: Cream 1080 square with serif header, a rule that draws in via scaleX, uppercase headline, blurb and a circular stamp that pops in with back.out(2) and slowly turns 20 degrees. Each seek draws the two-digit value (0 to 21, power3.out over 2.4s from 0.1D) crisp to an offscreen canvas at 720px, then samples it on a 15-degree rotated dot grid whose cell tightens 60 to 22px (power2.out) as the number resolves, drawing dots sized by coverage; a top-down wipe (reveal 0 to 1, expo.out) grows the dots in. At 0.71D the number scales 1.06 and settles with elastic.out(1,0.4); at 0.93D the reveal runs back to 0 and the copy fades.
adapt: Change TARGET, the header, headline, blurb and stamp strings, ink and paper colours; keep the cell 60 to 22 tightening and the 2.4s power3.out count.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas and the copy; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with an onUpdate on the state tweens that runs the halftone paint (the __fx.seek override). Scope '.rule', '.top', '.bot', '.stamp' to el; canvas is fixed 1080x1080.
caveats: per-frame getImageData on a 1080x1080 buffer plus thousands of sampled arcs is CPU heavy
canvas text uses Sharp Grotesk which must be loaded
